title: Bible Verses of Gratitude, and a Way to Keep a Thankfulness Record | Prayed
headline: Bible verses of gratitude, and how to keep a record that lasts
dek: Thirteen verses on giving thanks, arranged for the ordinary morning, the answered prayer, and the hard season when thanks is an act of will. With a prayer to write for each.
desc: Thirteen Bible verses of gratitude and thanksgiving from the World English Bible, arranged for the ordinary morning, the answered prayer, and the hard season when giving thanks is a decision. With a prayer to write for each.
card: Thirteen verses on giving thanks: the ordinary morning, the answered prayer, and the hard season.
intro: Gratitude is the easiest prayer to recommend and the hardest to sustain. Everyone agrees you should give thanks. Almost no one does it past the third day of a gratitude journal. The problem is not a lack of things to be thankful for. It is that thankfulness, unlike worry, does not remind you of itself.

The verses below are quoted word for word from the World English Bible and arranged for the three situations where thanks actually gets prayed: the ordinary morning when nothing is wrong, the day a prayer is answered, and the hard season when giving thanks is a decision rather than a feeling. The last group is the one that matters most and the one gratitude journals never mention.
Each group ends with a prayer you could write. The ordinary ones are worth keeping most, because they are the ones you will not remember.

paras: These are the verses for a day with nothing in it. Rain, coffee, the garden, the fact that everyone is home. Scripture treats the ordinary as a gift with a giver, and that is the whole shift.

verses.note: This is the day. Not a special one. Whichever one you are reading this on.
Every good gift. The small ones count, and they all have the same source.
Rain, rivers, grain. A verse for anyone with a garden, or a window.
A good thing. Giving thanks is not only a duty. It is good for the one doing it.

sections.pray: Thank you for a quiet morning. For the rain, for the coffee, for the fact that nothing is wrong today. I am writing this down because I will not remember it, and I want to.

paras: The moment of an answered prayer is the moment gratitude comes easily, and also the moment it evaporates fastest. Within a week the answer feels like it was always going to happen. These verses are about telling what God has done, out loud and on paper, before the memory softens.

verses.note: Tell of all your marvelous works. Telling is the verb. An answered prayer is meant to be recounted.
Don't forget all his benefits. The psalmist knows you will. That is why the verse exists.
The refrain of a psalm that lists, one after another, the people God rescued and what they were rescued from. A model for your own list.
Thanksgiving at the gates, praise in the courts. Thanks is the way in.

sections.pray: You answered. The scan was clear. I am writing it down today, while I still feel it, so that six months from now I cannot pretend it was luck. Thank you. I will tell someone.

paras: In everything give thanks, Paul writes, and he wrote it from a life that included prison and shipwreck. This is not gratitude as a mood. It is gratitude as a decision made in the dark, and these verses are the ones people hold onto when the feeling has gone.

verses.note: In everything. Not for everything. The thanks is given inside the hard thing, not about it.
From the book of Lamentations. Not consumed is the whole thanksgiving. Some seasons, that is enough.
Peace rules, and be thankful is attached to it. The two are given together.
With thanksgiving, in the same breath as the request. You can ask for the thing you do not have and give thanks in the same sentence. Paul did.
Always, concerning all things. The most demanding verse on this page, and the one that means the most in the year you can finally pray it.

sections.pray: I do not feel thankful and I am going to give thanks anyway. We are not consumed. That is what I have today. Thank you for that. Thank you for being here in the middle of this, since you have not taken it away.

closing_h2: Keep a record of what he has done
closing: The Psalms keep telling the reader to remember, and they keep telling it because remembering does not happen on its own. The ordinary mornings are forgotten. The answered prayers turn into things that were always going to work out. The hard seasons are survived and then the surviving is forgotten too.

The fix is not a gratitude journal, which most people abandon. It is a prayer journal that remembers for you. Prayed brings each written prayer back to you at three days, a week, a month and a year, so the thanks you wrote on a quiet Tuesday comes back in a hard December, and the prayer you marked answered builds into a timeline you can scroll on the days you cannot think of anything to be thankful for. Nothing you write leaves your phone.
Write one thank-you tonight, for something small. Date it. Let it come back to you when you need it.
